question: Termination-fee tail provision: what must happen during the tail period with respect to the same or a different acquisition proposal for the tail fee to be payable? (select all that apply)
options: Different Acquisition Proposal - Must be approved or not opposed (or another similar action) during Tail Period (no closing requirement)
Different Acquisition Proposal - Must be approved or not opposed (or another similar action) during Tail Period and transaction must close after Tail Period
Different Acquisition Proposal - Must sign during Tail Period (no closing requirement)
Different Acquisition Proposal - Must sign during Tail Period and close after Tail Period
Different Acquisition Proposal must close during Tail Period
Same Acquisition Proposal - Must be approved or not opposed (or another similar action) during Tail Period and transaction must close after Tail Period
Same Acquisition Proposal - Must be approved or not opposed to (or another similar action) during Tail Period (no closing requirement)
Same Acquisition Proposal - Must close during Tail Period
Same Acquisition Proposal - Must sign during Tail Period (no closing requirement)
Same Acquisition Proposal - Must sign during Tail Period and close after Tail Period
note: Typically one "Same" and one "Different" option apply.

question: Termination-fee tail provision: must the acquisition proposal have been publicly disclosed/announced (for at least one of the termination triggers)?
Termination-fee tail provision: for which termination triggers must the acquisition proposal have been publicly disclosed? (select all that apply)
options: “Publicly disclosed” requirement applies to Acquisition Proposal + Breach Trigger
“Publicly disclosed” requirement applies to Acquisition Proposal + No-Vote / MTC Failure Trigger
“Publicly disclosed” requirement applies to Acquisition Proposal + Outside Date Trigger
note: Breach Trigger = termination for Target breach; No-Vote / MTC Failure Trigger = termination for failure to obtain stockholder approval; Outside Date Trigger = termination at the outside/end date. Select only "No" if no public-disclosure requirement applies.

question: Termination-fee tail provision: must the acquisition proposal not have been withdrawn (still pending) at the time of termination or of the stockholder meeting (for at least one trigger)?
Termination-fee tail provision: length of the tail period?
note: "within 12 months" = a period of 12 months (one year) after termination.

question: What breaches by the Target preclude it from exercising its fiduciary termination right? (select all that apply)
options: (Material) breach of other provisions of agreement
Breach of no-shop resulting in a Superior Offer
Material breach of no-shop resulting in a Superior Offer

question: Buyer's matching right before the Target terminates to accept a Superior Offer (fiduciary termination right): length of the initial matching period?
Is a change of recommendation permitted on the basis of a board fiduciary determination alone (i.e., not tied to a Superior Offer or an Intervening Event)?
Is a change of recommendation permitted in response to an Intervening Event?
Does the agreement make the Target liable (e.g., deem it a breach by the Target) for no-shop violations by its Representatives?
What liability standard applies to the Target for no-shop violations by Representatives other than directors and officers?
note: "Strict liability" = any violation by such Representatives is deemed a breach by the Target; "Reasonable standard" = the Target is liable only if, e.g., it failed to use reasonable efforts to cause them to comply, or the Representative acted at the Target's direction.

question: Superior Offer definition: what percentage of the Target's stock must the proposal cover?
options: Greater than 50% but not "all or substantially all"
note: "50%" = the definition refers to 50% (e.g., "more than 50%" or "a majority"); "Greater than 50% but not all or substantially all" = e.g., 75% or 80%.

question: Superior Offer definition: what percentage of the Target's assets must the proposal cover?
options: Greater than 50% but not "all or substantially all"
note: Same scale as the stock-threshold question.

question: Type of merger consideration paid to Target stockholders?
Specific performance: are the parties "entitled to" specific performance, or only "entitled to seek" it?
